text:
Alex G: quick q on the embeddings endpoint contract — I noticed some clients sending {documents: [...] } instead of a raw string or [string]. Are we still accepting that wrapper? also how does truncation work now (per-item or per-batch)?
Maria T: we accept single string or list of strings officially. the {documents: ...} wrapper was tolerated for a while for legacy mobile clients but it's not in the spec and we should either document or deprecate it. truncation is per-item (we truncate each document to 8192 tokens by default). there is also a request-level token cap of 100k tokens currently — if you exceed that we return 413.
Kevin L: fwiw i've seen SDKs rely on the wrapper. suggest adding a soft-compat shim in the server that extracts `documents` if present and logs a deprecation warning, then update docs to call it out. also we should be explicit about input types: string | [string] only moving forward.
Julia R: ran into a failing test in CI that started after yesterday's runtime change. test log snippet:
```
FAIL tests/test_embeddings_contract.py::test_input_shape - ValueError: Invalid input shape: expected str or list[str]
```
CI Bot: build 2287 — tests failed in `eng-ml/embeddings` (see: https://ci.redwood.example/build/2287) :x:
Maria T: good catch @Julia R — can you paste the exact request body that triggered it? if it's the wrapper i'll push a compatibility PR tonight. planning to add a small unit test that keeps the legacy shape accepted for two minor releases then throws a warning.
Alex G: also need clarity on response format and ordering: do we guarantee output order matches input order? and what's the vector shape precisely? some downstream code expects `float32` arrays and errors on nulls.
Kevin L: yes, we guarantee order-preserving responses. response shape is a list of vectors: `[[f32,...], [f32,...], ...]` with dimension 1536 for the `text-embedding-small` model (varies by model). we return JSON arrays (not base64). no nulls for successful items; failed items will return an object with `error` for that index.
Maria T: pushing a PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/api-spec/pull/512 — adds compat shim + docs update + unit tests. pinging @Kevin L and @Alex G for review. I'll include an explicit example request/response snippet in the docs.
Alex G: thanks — example snippet i'd like included:
```
POST /v1/embeddings
Content-Type: application/json

# accepted shapes
{"input": "single string"}
{"input": ["doc1", "doc2"]}
{"documents": ["legacy doc1"]}  # compat only, will be deprecated

# example response
{
  "model": "text-embedding-small",
  "data": [
    {"embedding": [0.0012, -0.0034, ...]},
    {"embedding": [0.0023, 0.0041, ...]}
  ]
}
```
Kevin L: lgtm. note: max items per request is 1024. if someone needs larger batches recommend client-side chunking (we can add a helper in SDK).
Maria T: ok i'll merge the PR after tests pass. @Julia R can you re-run CI once the shim is merged to confirm your failing test is fixed? :thumbsup:
Julia R: will do, thanks everyone.
